answer: A bond-backed identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a comet that only shines while it carries real mass. Cheap fakes cannot multiply, because each new face costs locked capital that is slashed on fraud. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest, while an attacker flooding the market must fund an ember of capital for every fake identity, and karst-like, the ground gives way beneath identities that cannot pay.
